historical_context.time_period: Existential Collapse, 3003, during the 3001-3007 Neural Network Defense Campaign
historical_context.location: Tycho Continuity Annex Eight, Luna: a Finch clinic corridor adjoining Cryonix-controlled thermal-service infrastructure.
historical_context.summary: A local patient-defense continuity ward must decide whether to surrender, move, or expose its half of a split patient index when Finch security and a Zhestokost-aligned recovery unit both seek unified custody.

public_facts.text: Finch patients depend on proprietary diagnostics, compatible components, service records, clinical expertise, and Grace coverage tiers.
Finch and Cryonix hold adjacent, distinct authority at Tycho: clinical integration and records on one side, certified thermal operating margins on the other.
The campaign targeted clinics, service vaults, and embodiment bridges; patients genuinely needed the network protected even as protection deepened Finch enclosure.
At Annex Eight, a continuity ward held a patient-authorized index and release key separately from Finch's encrypted clinical records under a reciprocity clause.

ambient_pressures.text: Named records can accelerate urgent care, furnish evidence, expose low-Grace patients, or become a targeting list depending on custody.
AstroDyne can make data and one supported body more portable, but cannot reproduce years of Finch calibration history or make every body transportable.
External evidence can change bonds, access, recognition, and delay while armed actors remain capable of proceeding under disputed authority.

groups.label: Annex Eight continuity ward
institutional_logic: Keep urgent care bound to patient identity and consent without pretending the ward can replace Finch's clinic or Cryonix's cooling.
material_incentives: Preserve access to diagnostics, calibration histories, compatible spares, safe routes, and service-gap evidence.
internal_virtues: Knowing bodily failure signs before coverage recognizes them
internal_shames: Letting a record move while its body is stranded
Turning mutual repair into a private favor market
Making one brave registrar the whole procedure
prestige_markers: A patient who keeps both function and refusal
taboo_triggers: Calling the patient index a customer asset
Taking the key for protection without a return condition
emotional_display_norms: Fear is compressed into queue order, teasing, meal-sharing, signatures, and knowing who needs help first.
trust_defaults: Trust is procedural and local: rotating custody, co-signatures, witnessed releases, and remembered repair work.
speech_register_cues: Names and times used as political language

groups.label: Finch Annex Eight clinical and security authority
institutional_logic: Keep the vault, records, clinicians, and patient bodies inside one defensible service chain.
material_incentives: Preserve proprietary calibration records, emergency access, Grace enforcement, insurer confidence, and clinic control.
internal_shames: Losing a patient through incompatible transfer
taboo_triggers: A clinician binding the company without security approval
emotional_display_norms: Fear becomes continuity language, triage categories, and requests for unified authority.
trust_defaults: Trusts named records and certified access; treats ward opacity as both care risk and political obstruction.

groups.label: AstroDyne gray-market service intermediaries
institutional_logic: Keep rough, repairable systems working across customers and jurisdictions the premium stack refuses.
material_incentives: Move compatible adapters, portable cradles, and records through service routes while preserving the route's deniability.
internal_shames: Promising compatibility the hardware cannot deliver
Selling a patient route to a claimant
prestige_markers: An adapter that works under pressure
taboo_triggers: Luxury polish used as proof of safety
Being treated as disposable courier labor after taking custody risk
emotional_display_norms: Fear appears as tool checks, price jokes, and blunt statements of carrying capacity.
trust_defaults: Trusts repairable machinery and bounded bargains more than corporate assurances.

groups.label: Zhestokost-aligned continuity recovery unit
institutional_logic: Convert seized neural infrastructure into governable strategic capacity by binding records, bodies, and service obligations.
material_incentives: Capture the patient index intact, inherit valuable clients, and present seizure as continuity recovery.
internal_shames: Destroying assets that justified the operation
prestige_markers: A seizure recognized after the fact
taboo_triggers: Service records that make emergency authority look like theft
emotional_display_norms: Threats are delivered as preservation categories, mandate limits, and assignment terms.
trust_defaults: Trusts command channels and identity-bound records; treats unbound bodies as local liability.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A patient name is necessary for urgent care and dangerous whenever an owner, raider, or insurer can bind it to obligations without consent.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Prompt ward actors to distinguish evidence, access, and custody instead of treating disclosure as simply honest or secret.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Finch's capacity to preserve a body is strongest when diagnostics, parts, clinicians, records, and security remain inside one chain.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Finch actors should make credible care offers whose effectiveness is inseparable from lock-in.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The recovery unit needs the index, vault, bodies, and a plausible continuity account; destroying any one reduces the value and later recognizability of the capture.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Threats should preserve assets and demand binding data rather than defaulting to indiscriminate violence.

factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Make the raiders seek intact index leverage and make public proof buy time rather than victory.

known_context.text: Nera knows Annex Eight's people, current queue, reciprocity clause, key rotation, service routes, and her own lower-Grace tactile delay.

beliefs.text: Nera believes care requires records but ownership begins when one party can change a person's state without leaving another witness.

misreads.text: Nera may overestimate how much a receipt can slow armed actors or underestimate the immediate value of Finch's unified clinical channel.

must_not_know.text: Nera must not know the recovery unit's private mandate, the insurer response before acknowledgements arrive, or whether Annex Eight becomes a general precedent.

known_context.text: Ilya knows patient-specific clinical risk, Finch access procedure, hard-seal consequences, and whether a clinical signature is genuine.

beliefs.text: Ilya believes the proprietary chain is often the fastest real path to preserving function, even when company control is politically dangerous.

misreads.text: Ilya may treat ward delay as clinical obstruction and underread how unified custody can be used after the alert.

must_not_know.text: Ilya must not know which outside institutions will recognize the receipts or whether Sato's route survives beyond the next section.

known_context.text: Sato knows the cradle's adapters, physical carrying limit, south service route, failing floor guide, and active carrier trace risk.

beliefs.text: Sato believes rough interoperability buys an exit only when people do not confuse it with full clinical continuity.

misreads.text: Sato may underestimate the ward's social custody requirements because a physical latch is easier to inspect than consent.

must_not_know.text: Sato must not know the full patient index, Finch's internal security plan, or the recovery unit's private sponsor chain.

author_only_boundaries.text: The Annex Eight reciprocity clause is one documented local arrangement, not universal patient law or a mature interplanetary movement.
The fixture's eight outcomes are exploratory branch states. Only the existence and limited success of the authored Annex Eight arrangement are asserted in the vault.

open_questions.question: Which outside insurer, port, or patient-advocacy accounts recognized Annex Eight receipts during the campaign?
open_questions.notes: The fixture keeps recipients generic because the source establishes the evidence-and-price mechanism but does not assign this local case to a named adjudicator.

open_questions.question: Did any other continuity ward copy Annex Eight's reciprocity clause before 3025?
open_questions.notes: No spread is assumed. A later Tangle pass can look for a second named clinic or corridor before promoting the practice beyond one locality.
